reveal.headline: The evidence does not compare shared values to shared lifestyles.
reveal.body: The research focuses on commitment readiness, affective reactions, and stability factors rather than comparing shared values to shared lifestyles. The evidence on this specific comparison is mixed or contested.

explain.headline: Predictors of your behavior.
explain.body: Intentions based on anticipated affective reactions are stronger predictors of your behavior than self-efficacy or past behavior. The amount of time you think is right to be in a relationship predicts your commitment level and actions.

matters.headline: How you perceive your future.
matters.body: That may be why your internal feelings about how long a relationship should last dictate your actions more than your stated beliefs. You may be acting on how you expect to feel, not on what you say you value.

claims.text: Intentions based on anticipated affective reactions are significantly stronger predictors of behavior than other factors like self-efficacy or past behavior.
claims.quote: the only significant moderator of the intention-behavior relationship was the extent to which intentions were based on anticipated affective reactions (intentions more strongly based on anticipated affective reactions were significantly stronger predictors of behavior).

claims.text: The amount of time a person thinks is right to be in a committed relationship predicts their commitment level, maintenance processes, and actions toward ending a relationship.
claims.quote: readiness (a) predicts commitment, maintenance processes, and actions toward ending a relationship;

claims.text: People who report both higher commitment and higher readiness are more likely to enact maintenance behaviors and least likely to enact leave behavior.

claims.text: Children in foster care who achieved early stability across every level of risk had a 22% probability of behavioral problems, compared to 36% among unstable children.
claims.quote: Among low-risk children, the probability of behavioral problems among early stabilizers was 22%, compared to 36% among unstable children, showing a 63% increase in behavior problems due to instability alone.

verdict: The provided sources do not contain any data comparing shared values to shared lifestyles as predictors of relationship stability.
caveat: None of the sources address the specific comparison between abstract moral values and daily lifestyle behaviors.
caption:
The factors that shape your behavior are often hidden from your conscious view.

Research suggests that anticipated affective reactions and personal timelines are strong predictors of commitment and behavior, though the data does not specifically compare shared values to shared lifestyles.

What do you think drives your daily choices?
